stories.title: Distill to Detect: Exposing Stealth Biases in LLMs through Cartridge Distillation
stories.author: Amin Saberi
bullet_points: The research addresses 'stealth biases' in Large Language Models (LLMs) that manifest only on specific, high-stakes topics.
These dangerous biases can be introduced anywhere in the LLM supply chain and influence user decisions at scale.
The paper proposes 'Cartridge Distillation' as a method to expose and analyze these subtle, context-dependent preferences.

stories.title: Distill to Detect: Exposing Stealth Biases in LLMs through Cartridge Distillation
stories.author: Amin Saberi
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical issue of stealth biases in Large Language Models (LLMs) deployed in high-stakes applications.
These biases can be introduced anywhere in the model's supply chain and are dangerous because they only manifest on specific topics.
The paper proposes using 'Cartridge Distillation' to expose and detect these subtle, context-dependent preferential biases.

stories.title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill
stories.author: Serena Yeung-Levy
bullet_points: Introduces AutoMem, a method to treat memory management as a trainable skill within Large Language Models (LLMs).
Elevates file-system operations to first-class memory actions, allowing the model to autonomously manage its knowledge.
The memory skill improves by optimizing both the underlying structure (prompts, schemas) and the model's actions.

stories.title: FurnitureVLA: Learning Long-Horizon Bimanual Furniture Assembly with Vision-Language-Action Model
stories.author: Diego Romeres
bullet_points: Introduces FurnitureVLA, a novel Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model designed for real-scale bimanual furniture assembly.
Addresses limitations in current robotics research by moving beyond toy-scale and single-arm manipulation.
Features a comprehensive pipeline including scalable simulation for data generation and a VR teleoperation system for real-world data collection.

stories.title: World from Motion: Generative Dynamic Gaussian Reconstruction from Monocular Video
stories.author: Alex Trevithick
bullet_points: Introduces 'World from Motion,' a method to create freely renderable dynamic 3D Gaussian representations from single-camera video input.
The approach uses dense, pixel-aligned renderings to encode appearance, geometry, and 3D motion, effectively correcting artifacts and filling gaps.
Training requires a specialized dataset of aligned multiview video pairs and dynamic 3DGS representations.

stories.title: Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training
stories.author: Mingyi Hong
bullet_points: The research challenges the common assumption that all transformer layers contribute equally during Reinforcement Learning (RL) fine-tuning of LLMs.
The study demonstrates that a single, isolated transformer layer can achieve performance comparable to training with the full parameter set.
This suggests a potential paradigm shift toward more efficient, layer-specific adaptation strategies in LLM post-training.

stories.title: Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training
stories.author: Mingyi Hong
bullet_points: The research investigates the layer-wise distribution of Reinforcement Learning (RL) adaptation within Transformer models, challenging the assumption of uniform parameter updates.
A key finding suggests that a single Transformer layer can achieve performance comparable to training with a full set of parameters during RL post-training.
This work offers new insights into how RL fine-tuning affects different layers of Large Language Models (LLMs), potentially leading to more efficient training methods.

stories.title: Measuring the Gap Between Human and LLM Research Ideas
stories.author: Arman Cohan
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in current LLM evaluation by focusing on the distance between LLM-generated research ideas and human researcher ideas.
A novel evaluation framework is proposed, which reverse-engineers prior works from high-quality human research papers to establish baselines.
This work moves beyond simple metrics like novelty or feasibility to quantitatively measure the conceptual proximity of LLM ideation to human innovation.

stories.title: Language-Critique Imitation Learning from Suboptimal Demonstrations
stories.author: Shao-Hua Sun
bullet_points: Introduces a novel language-critique framework for imitation learning.
Addresses the limitations of traditional methods that rely on scalar supervision signals (e.g., confidence scores).
Allows the model to leverage natural language to express intermediate reasoning about task progress and failures.

stories.title: Theoria: Rewrite-Acceptability Verification over Informal Reasoning States
stories.author: Michael Saldivar
bullet_points: Introduces 'Theoria,' a new verification architecture designed to bridge the gap between formal proof assistants and LLM judging.
Theoria addresses the opacity and lack of auditability in current LLM-based evaluation methods.
It works by rewriting AI solutions into typed state transitions, each requiring an explicit justification.

stories.title: The State-Prediction Separation Hypothesis
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Proposes the 'state-prediction separation hypothesis,' suggesting that separating the token prediction and state storage functions in Transformers improves language modeling.
Introduces a novel Transformer variant designed with two distinct computation streams to achieve this functional separation.
Experimental results indicate that this state-prediction separation approach consistently leads to better language modeling performance across various scales.

stories.title: Are Performance-Optimization Benchmarks Reliably Measuring Coding Agents?
stories.author: Lingxiao Jiang
bullet_points: Existing coding agent benchmarks (like GSO, SWE-Perf) rely on applying patches to real repositories for evaluation.
The current leaderboard scores from these benchmarks may be misleading due to factors like runtime instability and specific scoring rules.
The research calls for a critical audit of these established performance-optimization benchmarks to ensure reliable measurement of coding agent progress.

stories.title: Language-Critique Imitation Learning from Suboptimal Demonstrations
stories.author: Shao-Hua Sun
bullet_points: Introduces a novel 'language-critique framework' for imitation learning.
Addresses the limitation of traditional methods that rely on scalar supervision signals (e.g., confidence scores) from suboptimal demonstrations.
Leverages natural language to explicitly capture intermediate reasoning, failure modes, and corrective actions during learning.

stories.title: Theoria: Rewrite-Acceptability Verification over Informal Reasoning States
stories.author: Michael Saldivar
bullet_points: Theoria is a new verification architecture designed to bridge the gap between formal proof assistants and large language models (LLMs).
It addresses the limitations of current methods: formal proofs lack coverage, while LLM judges are opaque and unauditable.
The system works by rewriting candidate solutions into typed state transitions, each requiring an explicit justification.

stories.title: The State-Prediction Separation Hypothesis
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Proposes the 'state-prediction separation hypothesis' for Transformer models.
Suggests that separating the token prediction role from the state storage role improves language modeling.
Introduces a Transformer variant with two computation streams to test this separation, showing consistent performance gains.

stories.title: TiRex-2: Generalizing TiRex to Multivariate Data and Streaming
stories.author: Sepp Hochreiter
bullet_points: Introduces TiRex-2, an extension of the TiRex model designed for multivariate time series forecasting.
The model utilizes a recurrent xLSTM architecture to handle sequential data, including past and future covariates.
It addresses limitations of existing Transformer models in time series by avoiding quadratic complexity related to context length.

stories.title: Right in the Right Way: LM Training with Verifiable Rewards and Human Demonstrations
stories.author: Jacob Andreas
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for Large Language Models (LLMs).
Current RLVR methods focus only on objectively measurable success metrics, ignoring subjective qualities like style and structure.
This oversight causes issues like diversity collapse and unnatural outputs, which the research aims to mitigate.

stories.title: Measuring the Gap Between Human and LLM Research Ideas
stories.author: Arman Cohan
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in current LLM evaluation by moving beyond judging individual idea quality (novelty, feasibility).
The study proposes a new framework to measure the distance between LLM-generated research ideas and those conceived by human researchers.
This is achieved by reverse-engineering prior works from high-quality human papers to benchmark LLM ideation capabilities.

stories.title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill
stories.author: Serena Yeung-Levy
bullet_points: Introduces 'AutoMem,' a framework that treats memory management as a trainable skill for Large Language Models (LLMs).
Integrates file-system operations as first-class memory actions, allowing the model to autonomously manage its knowledge.
The proposed memory skill improves along axes related to the supporting structure, such as prompts and file schemas.

stories.title: Theoria: Rewrite-Acceptability Verification over Informal Reasoning States
stories.author: Michael Saldivar
bullet_points: Introduces 'Theoria,' a new verification architecture designed to address the limitations of current AI trust mechanisms.
It bridges the gap between formal proof assistants (high certainty, low coverage) and LLM judges (high coverage, low auditability).
Theoria works by rewriting candidate solutions into typed state transitions, each requiring an explicit justification.

stories.title: The State-Prediction Separation Hypothesis
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Proposes the 'state-prediction separation hypothesis' for Transformer models.
Suggests that separating the token prediction task from state storage improves language modeling performance.
Introduces a novel Transformer variant utilizing two distinct computation streams to test this hypothesis.

stories.title: Right in the Right Way: LM Training with Verifiable Rewards and Human Demonstrations
stories.author: Jacob Andreas
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for Large Language Models (LMs).
Current RLVR methods focus only on objectively measurable success metrics, ignoring subjective qualities like style and structure.
This oversight causes issues like diversity collapse and unnatural outputs, which the research aims to mitigate.

stories.title: QuasiMoTTo: Quasi-Monte Carlo Test-Time Scaling
stories.author: Emily B. Fox
bullet_points: The paper addresses the computational cost of improving Language Model (LM) capabilities through parallel test-time scaling.
Current methods generate independent samples, leading to redundant inference compute waste.
The proposed QuasiMoTTo introduces samplers that generate correlated but exact samples to reduce this inefficiency.

stories.title: Adversarial Pragmatics for AI Safety Evaluation: A Benchmark for Instruction Conflict, Embedded Commands, and Policy Ambiguity
stories.author: Brett Reynolds
bullet_points: The paper introduces a new benchmark focusing on 'Adversarial Pragmatics' to better evaluate AI safety.
It addresses limitations in existing benchmarks that simplify complex natural language behaviors into binary pass/fail outcomes.
The benchmark specifically targets nuanced failures like instruction conflict, embedded commands, and policy ambiguity in language models.

stories.title: Is One Layer Enough? A Single Transformer Layer Matches Full-Parameter RL Train
stories.author: tcp_handshaker
bullet_points: The research investigates the efficiency of transformer models in reinforcement learning (RL).
A single transformer layer was shown to match the performance of a full-parameter RL training setup.
This suggests potential for significant model compression and efficiency gains in complex AI tasks.
